name: Observer azed crossword No 2,584
preamble: Apart from 20, every entry is formed by cutting a word or words at any point and then reattaching the two parts, the second followed by the first, e.g. WORD could give ORDW, RDWO or DWOR. Clues consist of a definition of the unmutilated answer and a subsidiary indication of the grid entry. 20 (a verb form, to be deduced) appears as normal. Competitors should submit with their entries a clue to this word, cut wherever they choose, following the style of all the other clues. Please indicate clearly where your clue cuts the unmutilated word. Every entry is in The Chambers Dictionary (2014) except one proper name.

solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seasonal postal item: cosmetic colouring mostly damaged shirt (about 600) (13, two words)

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the cosmetic is dropped
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the shirt's letters, with the extras, are rearranged

blocks.note: mascara is a cosmetic that colours the eyelashes
c. (circa) means about
D is 500 in Roman numerals, and with the C of about it makes DC, 600
taken as written

explanation.surface: A make-up mishap: someone's mascara has ruined their shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle the definition is of the whole word, CHRISTMAS CARD, while the wordplay builds the grid entry MASCARDCHRIST, the word cut after CHRIST and its halves swapped. C (about) and D together make DC, 600 in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting card sent through the post at the festive season is the classic seasonal mailing.

clue.text: Wrongly calculate partner's gambling stake – it's raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read from the bottom upwards, so the last words run backwards

blocks.note: a mate is a partner
mise is a stake or wager in gambling
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler admits their partner's bet has been miscalculated after it was increased.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of MISESTIMATE; the wordplay gives the grid entry MATEMISESTI, cut after MIS and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To misestimate is to judge an amount wrongly, a direct synonym for miscalculating.

clue.text: River fish died, overcome by skill

blocks.note: art is skill
d. is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A river fish perished, beaten by an angler's skill.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'overcome by' puts the skill word on top. The definition is of DART; the grid shows ARTD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dart is an old name for the dace, a small freshwater fish of rivers.

clue.text: Thinks force must be limited to opportune time locally

indicators.note: being limited to something means being confined within it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: seel is a dialect word for a favourable season or time
F is the symbol for force

explanation.surface: Someone believes force should be used only when the moment is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' flags a dialect word. The definition is of FEELS; the grid entry is SFEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel something is to believe or hold it as an opinion, so feels matches thinks.

clue.text: Passage to bear in course of wild rant

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of rant run out of control into a new order
something happening in the course of another sits in the middle of it

blocks.note: taken as written
to sit (through) something is to endure or bear it

explanation.surface: Someone has to put up with a passage of a furious tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of TRANSIT; the grid entry ANSITTR is that word cut after TR and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is passage or conveyance from one place to another.

clue.text: Sacred plant representation depicted in artistic diploma

indicators.note: a picture depicted in something sits within it, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: DA is a Diploma in Art
a map is a representation of an area

explanation.surface: An art student's diploma piece shows a holy plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of PADMA; the grid entry DMAPA is that word cut after PA and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Padma is the lotus, a flower held sacred in Hindu and Buddhist tradition.

clue.text: Ancient Greek region after college excited the artist

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so the letters of the little word are jumbled

blocks.note: C is an abbreviation for college
the word the, its letters rearranged
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist is thrilled about an ancient Greek region after leaving college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After college' sets the college letter first. The definition is of THRACE; the grid entry CETHRA is that word cut after THRA and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was the ancient region north of the Aegean, home to the Thracians in Greek history.

clue.text: There's a dash of alcohol in this tea

indicators.note: a dash is the smallest splash, so only the opening letter of the drink is used
in places the splash inside the Latin word

blocks.note: hic is Latin for this
the opening letter of alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone admits their tea has been laced with a drop of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of CHAI; the grid entry HAIC is that word cut after C and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Chai is a word for tea, especially spiced Indian milky tea.

clue.text: Ingredient in veggie cookery, concentrated, without a name

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the word

blocks.note: intense means concentrated or strong
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A vegetarian recipe uses a concentrated ingredient with no brand name.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of SEITEN; the grid entry ITENSE is that word cut after SE and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Seitan (or seiten) is wheat gluten used as a meat substitute in vegetarian dishes.

clue.text: As I changed inside that will do as an alternative

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the two short words have their letters rearranged
inside places the rearranged letters within the following word

blocks.note: so! is an interjection meaning that will do, enough
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that a change made inside will do as a stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of OSSIA, a musical direction; the grid entry SSIAO is that word cut after O and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossia is an Italian musical term marking an optional alternative passage, meaning 'or'.

clue.text: Careless campin' had briefly got pitched among cattle once

indicators.note: something pitched among others is set down in their midst, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: tentin' is tenting with the dropped final G the apostrophe shows
aver is an archaic word for a draught beast, cattle
'd is the shortened form of had

explanation.surface: A sloppy camper briefly pitched a tent in a field of cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of INADVERTENT; the grid entry TENTINADVER is that word cut after INADVER and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Inadvertent means unintended through lack of attention, so careless is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Maximum sentence? Left inside, passion rises

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means being read upwards, so the word for passion runs backwards
inside places the abbreviation for left within the other piece

blocks.note: fire is passion or ardour
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A judge, given a whole-life term, sees passion flare up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of LIFER; the grid entry ERLIF is that word cut after LIF and the halves swapped. The question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifer can be a life sentence itself, the heaviest term a court can impose.

clue.text: Extra label chap reversed disguised age

indicators.note: reversed turns the word for chap back to front
something disguised has its appearance altered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a man is a chap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man lies about his age with a false name tag.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of AGNAME; the grid entry NAMEAG is that word cut after AG and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: An agname is an additional name or epithet tacked on to a person's ordinary name.

clue.text: Splosh, reverse of fitting, cut short within

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word written back to front
cut means trimmed, so the word for short loses its last letter
within places the trimmed word inside the backwards one

blocks.note: apt means fitting
terse means short, curt

explanation.surface: A splash lands somewhere unsuitable, interrupting things.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of SPATTER; the grid entry TTERSPA is that word cut after SPA and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To splosh and to spatter both describe splashing liquid about noisily.

clue.text: Number I issue, with backing, small and cosy

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the run of pieces is read in reverse

blocks.note: N is short for number
taken as written
to emit is to issue

explanation.surface: A magazine's first number comes with support for a snug little venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of INTIME; the grid entry TIMEIN is that word cut after IN and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Intime, borrowed from French, describes a place that is intimate, compact and homely.

clue.text: Eastern purveyor of cheese etc Germany suppressed

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
a deli sells cheese, cold meats and the like
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: An Eastern seller of cheese and other foods has been shut down in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suppressed' looks like part of a story about the shop, but it is the definition, of ELIDED; the grid entry EDELID is that word cut after EL and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To elide is to omit or strike out, as with a sound or passage, so elided means suppressed.

clue.text: Fish? Cross having to return number caught

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, so the abbreviation is placed within the cross
to return is to go back, so the whole is read backwards

blocks.note: a tau is a T-shaped cross
N is short for number

explanation.surface: An angler is annoyed at having to throw back the number of fish caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of TUNA; the grid entry UNAT is that word cut after T and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuna is a large ocean fish, so it is an example of what the question mark allows.

clue.text: Assault rifle – I rage following pain

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the word it governs is placed behind the word for pain

blocks.note: mal is French for pain or ache
taken as written
to tear about is to rage

explanation.surface: A gunman says he rages after the hurt, with an assault rifle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following pain' sets the pain word first. The definition is of ARMALITE; the grid entry MALITEAR is that word cut after AR and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: The ArmaLite is a lightweight automatic rifle, the type used as an assault weapon.

clue.text: Exhaust twisted deep, obstruction inside

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters of deep are rearranged
inside places the obstruction within the rearranged letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A car's twisted exhaust pipe has a blockage deep inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' reads as a car part but is the verb, defining DEPLETE; the grid entry EPLETED is that word cut after D and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete a supply is to use it up, which is what exhausting it means.

clue.text: Growing medium orchestra requires leader for inspiration

indicators.note: a leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra
the opening letter of inspiration

explanation.surface: An orchestra needs a conductor to inspire it to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of SOIL; the grid entry LSOI is that word cut after SOI and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil is the earth in which plants are grown, the gardener's basic medium.

clue.text: See preamble

blocks.note: surface reading: the solver is sent to the instructions instead of being given a clue
setter's reading: the preamble says this entry is a verb form to be deduced from the grid, entered uncut, and that competitors write their own clue to it

explanation.walkthrough: This is the competition word: no clue is printed, and its letters come from the crossings. It fits the Christmas theme of wrapping presents and is the only entry not cut and rejoined.
explanation.definitionFit: Gift-wrapped is the past tense of the verb to gift-wrap, to pack a present in decorative paper.

clue.text: One of many downed at the Gabba boozer, that is before time

definitions.text: One of many downed at the Gabba

blocks.note: a boozer is a pub, an inn
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: At a cricket ground pub, the drinking goes on before closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gabba is the cricket ground in Brisbane, Australia. The definition is of TINNIE, Australian slang for a can of beer; the grid entry INNIET is that word cut after T and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinnie is a can of beer in Australia, so many are drunk by spectators at a cricket match there.

clue.text: Our set was working with special retort

blocks.note: we are our group, ourselves
a machine that ran was working
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Our crowd was busy coming up with a particularly good comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of ANSWER; the grid entry WERANS is that word cut after ANS and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp reply, which is a kind of answer.

clue.text: Tasty slice of delicatessen consumed in Italian city

indicators.note: a slice is a small piece cut from the front, so only the opening letter of the shop is used
something consumed in another has gone inside it

blocks.note: Pisa is a city in Tuscany
the opening letter of delicatessen

explanation.surface: A delicious slice of deli meat was eaten in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of SAPID; the grid entry PIDSA is that word cut after SA and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid means having a pleasant flavour, a literary word for savoury.

clue.text: Member of family taking on university duty

blocks.note: a son is a family member
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: One of the family takes on responsibility for going to college.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of ONUS; the grid entry SONU is that word cut after ONU and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility, a duty that falls on someone.

clue.text: Computer expert, spy carelessly breaking bone

indicators.note: carelessly suggests the letters of spy are thrown together in a new order
breaking into something means getting inside it

blocks.note: os is Latin for bone, used in anatomy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tech whiz turned spy breaks a bone through carelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of SYSOP; the grid entry OPSYS is that word cut after SYS and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A sysop is a system operator, the person who runs a computer system or bulletin board.

clue.text: Chunk of a meteor landed in O'Hare, exploding

indicators.note: an exploding thing is blown apart, so the airport name's letters are scattered and rearranged
in places the word for landed inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: taken as written
lit is a past tense of light, to land or alight

explanation.surface: A lump of a meteor has come down at Chicago's O'Hare airport and blown up.
explanation.walkthrough: O'Hare is Chicago's main airport. The definition is of AEROLITH; the grid entry EROLITHA is that word cut after A and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerolith is a stony meteorite, a piece of a meteor that reaches the ground.

clue.text: Fillet maybe served in trattoria's tariff

indicators.note: something served in a dish is contained in it, so the letters are found within the words that follow

blocks.note: found spanning the end of trattoria's and the start of tariff

explanation.surface: A fillet steak is on the menu at an Italian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fillet' wants to be a cut of meat; it is the architectural sense. The definition is of STRIA; the grid entry RIAST is that word cut after ST and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture a stria is a fillet, the flat band between the flutes of a column.

clue.text: Tense before race strangely, take a sudden fall after mounting

definitions.text: take a sudden fall after mounting

indicators.note: strangely means oddly, so the letters of race are rearranged

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for tense in grammar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jockey is nervous before an odd race and takes a tumble after getting on the horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounting' suggests getting on a horse; it means rising, of prices. The definition is of REACT; the grid entry TREAC is that word cut after REAC and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: On the stock exchange, prices are said to react when they drop after a rise.

clue.text: Part of traditional Burns night? A wee bittie sleep needed

indicators.note: a wee bittie is Scots for a small piece, so only a small part of the following words is taken

blocks.note: found spanning the end of sleep and the start of needed

explanation.surface: On Burns night a Scot needs a little sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns night (25 January) celebrates the poet Robert Burns with haggis, neeps and tatties. The definition is of NEEP, Scots for a turnip; the grid entry EPNE is that word cut after NE and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Neeps (mashed swede or turnip) are the traditional accompaniment to haggis at a Burns supper.

clue.text: Scots bury beloved, end given priority

indicators.note: giving the end priority means moving the last letter to the front

blocks.note: dear means beloved

explanation.surface: Scots lay a loved one to rest, putting the end first.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of EARD, Scots for to bury; the grid entry RDEA is that word cut after EA and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Eard is a Scots verb meaning to inter or put in the earth, from eard meaning earth.

clue.text: Pike to disentangle? Special net required

blocks.note: ged is a Scots word for the pike fish
red (redd) is a dialect verb meaning to clear or disentangle

explanation.surface: An angler asks how to untangle a pike from a special net.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of DREDGE; the grid entry GEDRED is that word cut after DRE and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredge is a bag-shaped dragnet used to scoop oysters and the like from the seabed.

clue.text: Greek bust, what takes little room within

indicators.note: takes means admits or accepts, so the short word holds the abbreviation inside

blocks.note: eh? is a request to repeat, meaning what?
rm is the abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: Someone asks what Greek statue fits in a small space.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of HERM; the grid entry ERMH is that word cut after H and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A herm is a Greek pillar topped with a carved head, originally of Hermes.

clue.text: Sort of rabbit dies horribly in it

indicators.note: horribly suggests something mangled, so the letters of dies are rearranged
in places the rearranged letters inside the word for it

blocks.note: it in the sense of sex appeal is SA
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rabbit of some breed meets a gruesome end.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of DASSIE, the rock rabbit or hyrax of Africa; the grid entry SSIEDA is that word cut after DA and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: The dassie is called the rock rabbit, though it is a hyrax, not a true rabbit.

clue.text: Member of staff, one opposed to inaction having retired

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the words before it are read in reverse

blocks.note: an means one
v. (versus) means against, opposed to
rest is inactivity

explanation.surface: A staff member who disliked idleness has finally retired.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of SERVANT; the grid entry ANTSERV is that word cut after SERV and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant is employed in a household, one of its domestic staff.

clue.text: I'll be replaced by soprano in psalm voice in certain parts

indicators.note: being replaced means one letter is swapped out for another

blocks.note: the Venite is Psalm 95, sung at morning prayer
S is the abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A singer says a soprano will take their place in a psalm.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is of STEVEN, a dialect word for voice; 'in certain parts' means regionally. The grid entry VENSTE is that word cut after STE and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Steven is a Scots and northern English word for a voice or loud call.

clue.text: This time accepting church mass it tried being converted

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the abbreviation is held inside the rearranged letters
something converted is changed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A churchgoer attempted mass, and was converted to the faith this time.
explanation.walkthrough: This was the Christmas puzzle, so 'This time' is the season it appeared. The definition is of CHRISTMASTIDE; the grid entry ISTMASTIDECHR is that word cut after CHR and the halves swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmastide is the festive season, the time of year when the puzzle was published.
